ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: Gimme Some Slack
ModMetaData.author: Mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Drawn flexible pipes and wires to better display simple circuit-like plans underneath.
Cables: the conduit itself becomes invisible and keeps working exactly like vanilla conduit. A purely cosmetic layer reads the conduit network as a graph of the things it connects (generators, batteries, machines, junctions, the places where it disappears into a wall or rock and comes out again) and draws loose, too-long cords between connected neighbours over the walkable floor. Cords never cross a wall and never join two things that are not really connected. Breaks read at a glance: a conduit end still on a powered net sparks; a dead end lies limp. Nothing of theirs is saved, so adding or removing the mod mid-game is safe for them; the power overlay's connection lines are left alone.
Overhead lines: masts, lamp masts and wall brackets carry real power over open ground on sagging overhead wires that sway in the wind and may pass over roofed rooms. A cut or orphaned wire hangs from its insulator down to the break and sparks while live; explosions can cut a wire. A power-tap clamp quietly drains another faction's grid into yours without merging the two. Unlike the cords these are real buildings with saved links: removing the mod from a save that holds them loses them, with missing-definition errors.
Flexible hoses: thick, stiff hoses laid from a hose reel, flat when empty and plump while liquid flows, bound at both ends with dense cloth wraps.
Four looks, switched together in Mod Settings: Scrapper, Industrial, Modern and Futuristic. Everything lives in ONE Mod Settings entry with three tabs (Cables, Overhead lines, Flexible hoses); every behaviour has a switch, and each master switch brings the vanilla art back at once.
